text:
priya: Quick sync — need to lock the Rank/Scoring API contract for Q2. Customers keep asking for flexible top_k, normalized scores, and predictable truncation behavior. I'll collect decisions here.

mario: +1. Are we adding a standalone /v1/rank or extending /v1/completions? Customers want a lightweight rerank path for candidate arrays.

sarah: leaning standalone /v1/rank. Keeps contracts explicit and avoids bloating general completions payloads. Request shape: content (query), candidates: [{id, text, metadata}].

anita: from UX: designers need a stable, normalized score by default (0-1) so UIs don't need to guess. But allow raw scores for advanced users.

priya: proposal: default "normalized" to 0-1 via minmax. Add opt-out query param `raw_scores=true`. top_k default 10, max 100. Server-side candidate-side truncation (truncate candidate text to token limit) and return a warning header if truncation happened.

mario: we should support normalization choices: `minmax`, `zscore`, `softmax`. Implementation note: softmax for logits, minmax for arbitrary score ranges. Also include both `score` (raw) and `normalized_score` in response when applicable.

sarah: implementation details: for softmax use log-sum-exp to avoid overflow. Perf target: p95 < 80ms for 10 candidates on dedicated infra, <200ms on hosted medium tier. If we can't hit that, require fallback to async or coarser defaults.

bruce: (from a customer thread) fintech client needs deterministic stable sorting across SDK versions and tie-breakers. They also want candidate_id preserved and a deterministic tie-break by id and optional seed.

anita: +1 to deterministic tie-break. Also request an opt-in `debug: true` mode that returns score_distribution and per-candidate token-lengths for QA.

priya: launch checklist draft: API spec + examples, SDK updates, canary plan, perf benchmarks (throughput + p95), regression evals on canonical prompt set, and acceptance tests. Acceptance criteria: contract v1 doc, SDKs return normalized scores by default, perf SLOs met on dedicated, warnings for truncation documented.

sarah: edge cases: empty candidates -> 400 with helpful message. Overlong candidate text -> auto-truncate to candidate_token_limit (configurable) and set response header `X-Rank-Warning: truncated-candidates`. For too many candidates (>100) -> 413 or slice? prefer 413 with guidance to paginate.

mario: open question: pairwise / matrix scoring customers want pairwise outputs. I'd propose v1 scalar-only (score per candidate), and put pairwise/matrix as v2 roadmap for Q3.

priya: decision recorded: v1 supports scalar scores only. Response fields: `candidate_id`, `score` (raw when available), `normalized_score` (0-1 by default), optional `explanation` string, and `metadata` passthrough. `raw_scores=true` returns only `score`. `normalization` param can be `minmax|zscore|softmax`.

anita: UX note: normalized default makes immediate adoption easier for dashboards. For debugging include `score_distribution` when `debug=true`.

sarah: sample request body (v1):
```json
{
  "query": "how to reset password",
  "candidates": [
    {"id":"c1","text":"Reset via settings > account"},
    {"id":"c2","text":"Use forgot password link"}
  ],
  "top_k": 5,
  "normalization": "minmax",
  "debug": false
}
```

mario: perf/implementation notes: compute scores in float32, only cast to float64 for zscore variance calc if needed. For streaming/large candidate lists, do early top_k selection heuristics to avoid scoring everything when max_candidates huge.

bruce: acceptance from CS: if we include deterministic tie-break + truncation warning + SDK examples, a few customers will onboard early. Please include migration notes.

priya: timeline: spec + docs by next Tue (1833490000), SDK samples + integration tests by end of sprint, canary on dedicated after perf signoff. Pairwise queued for Q3.
deploy-bot: canary job scheduled for 1833460800 — will post status in #deploys.

sarah: will open PR with API proto + server stub today. I'll add the truncation header and tie-break logic to the spec.

priya: thanks — I'll collate this into an RFC and tag owners. If anyone has strong objections to minmax default or candidate-truncate-first rule, call it out here. Otherwise I'll move forward with this scope for v1.
